source.author: verg
source.text: Tum mihi prima genas vestibat flore iuventas, mirabarque duces Teucros, mirabar et ipsum Laomedontiaden, sed cunctis altior ibat Anchises: mihi mens iuvenali ardebat amore compellare virum et dextrae coniungere dextram.
source.text_original: Tum mihi prima genas vestibat flore iuventas, / mirabarque duces Teucros, mirabar et ipsum / Laomedontiaden, sed cunctis altior ibat / Anchises: mihi mens iuvenali ardebat amore / compellare virum et dextrae coniungere dextram.
source.text_english: Then my first youth was clothing my cheeks with bloom, and I marveled at the Teucrian leaders, I marveled at Laomedon’s own son himself, but Anchises went taller than all the rest: my mind was burning with youthful desire to address the man and to join right hand with right hand.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: hinc laevom Telamon pelagus tenet, altior inde occupat Alcides aliud mare, cetera pubes dividitur: celer Asterion, quem matre cadentem Piresius gemino fovit pater amne Cometes, segnior Apidani vires ubi sentit Enipeus.
reuse.text_original: hinc laevom Telamon pelagus tenet, altior inde / occupat Alcides aliud mare, cetera pubes / dividitur: celer Asterion, quem matre cadentem / Piresius gemino fovit pater amne Cometes, / segnior Apidani vires ubi sentit Enipeus.
reuse.text_english: From here Telamon holds the sea to the left; from there Alcides occupies the other sea from a higher place. The rest of the young men are divided: swift Asterion, whom Piresius, his father, as he was falling, nourished with twin rivers, and slower Enipeus, where he feels the strength of the Apidanus.
